text:
Sophia Ramirez: Hey team — quick onboarding Qs: I just submitted benefits enrollment but realized I need to add my domestic partner. Do I upload proof now? When will deductions start? Also, my first paycheck appears to be prorated — is that expected? And what's the process to submit moving/relocation expense receipts for reimbursement?
Alex T: @Sophia Ramirez welcome! For partner add, tag @Jen (People Ops) here. Payroll proration is expected if you started mid-pay-cycle. Moving receipts go through Expensify and we tag them for people-ops.
Jen (People Ops): Hi @Sophia — short answers: 1) Add a dependent in the benefits portal and upload the domestic partner affidavit + proof of shared residence (utility bill, joint lease, or bank stmt). 2) Effective date: most carriers make coverage effective the 1st of the month after enrollment is confirmed. If you enrolled within 30 days of hire some carriers allow retroactive coverage — we'll check. 3) Payroll deductions begin the first pay period after benefits become effective, so a mid-cycle hire often sees a prorated first check. 4) Moving/relocation reimbursements: submit receipts in Expensify under the 'Relocation - People Ops' policy and include your offer letter reference. We typically process within 1–2 pay cycles after approval. Internal links: benefits portal — https://benefits.redwood.internal/, Expensify instructions — https://confluence.redwood.internal/relocation-expense.
Sophia Ramirez: Thanks! I uploaded the affidavit and a lease PDF to the portal just now. How will I know if carriers accepted it or if you need anything else?
Jen (People Ops): I see the upload — thanks for doing that. I'll verify with the carrier tomorrow morning. If anything is missing I'll DM you directly and post an update here. If accepted, we'll mark enrollment confirmed and payroll will queue deductions.
Payroll Bot: Payroll system note: New-hire proration applies. Estimated pay date for first run: 2026-04-02.
Alex T: Quick follow — if Sophia has any urgent out-of-pocket moving expenses we can approve an advance. @Jen is that still our procedure?
Jen (People Ops): Yes — we can do a relocation advance. Sophia, file a ticket to the people-ops queue titled "Relocation advance" with the receipts and amount requested. We try to respond within 24 business hours.
Sophia Ramirez: Will do. Thanks everyone for the fast help. :thumbsup:
Jen (People Ops): Looping back — carrier confirmed the dependent docs this afternoon. Coverage effective 2026-05-01. Payroll: deductions will start the first pay period after 2026-05-01 so you'll see proration reflected on the April paycheck only. Moving reimbursement for $850 approved; it will be coded and paid on the next payroll run. Ping me if anything changes or you don't see the reimbursement on the expected date.
